scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

So, the person in question is a 21-year-old woman who gave her two cousins, Tj (15) and Ked (13), iPhones when the new models were released. Ked had been stealing money from some extended family members, and he admitted to it. There was a fight, and Ked's parents defended him, not caring that he was stealing and cutting off the extended family. During winter break, Ked apologized and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic, refusing to admit they were wrong and hating the extended family now.

The extended family hosted a housewarming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to go, but their parents told Ked he couldn't go in case the extended family accused him of stealing again. Tj was told he could do whatever he wanted and that his parents trusted him to make the right decision. So, Tj went to the sleepover, while Ked stayed home.

When Tj arrived at the party, his phone started blowing up with texts from his parents yelling at him for coming to the extended family's house. They called him a disappointment, said they trusted him to make the right decision and he failed, and that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. Tj asked to be left out of the drama, but his parents repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home, they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for two weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he never got punished. The person is disgusted by how the parents are raising their kids and has lost all respect for them.

She told them that while she can't control how they discipline their children, it's not their property to take away from him, and she won't go behind their back and let him use the phone. But since it was her gift to him, she'd like to hold onto it until the two weeks are up. The narcissistic parents made a big deal, and other extended family members are telling her she should've stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want. She's only asking for the phone to be in her possession because she thinks they're treating him unfairly. Everyone agrees the parents are horrible. If they were decent parents and punishing him fairly, she wouldn't have asked for the phone back. She may be the asshole because she asked for the phone back because she felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules. So, she decided to take some of their "power" away by asking for her gift back.

Now, I need to evaluate whether her action is morally acceptable or not. Let's break it down.

First, she gave the phone as a gift to Tj. Legally, once the gift is given, it's his property. However, she's taking it back because she feels the parents are treating him unfairly. She's not trying to control him but to take away some of the parents' power over him.

On one hand, she's respecting Tj's ownership of the phone by not letting him use it while it's with her. She's not hiding it or using it herself; she's just holding onto it until the two weeks are up. On the other hand, she's interfering in how the parents discipline their child, which could be seen as overstepping.

But considering the parents are described as horrible, stubborn, narcissistic, and unfair, especially since Ked admitted to stealing and wasn't punished, while Tj is being punished for making his own decision to attend the party, it seems like the parents are indeed treating their children unfairly.

She's not taking the phone to control Tj but to prevent the parents from using it as a tool of punishment. She's standing up for Tj, who is being treated cruelly by his parents. By taking back the phone, she's reducing the parents' ability to control Tj through the punishment of taking away his phone.

However, some might argue that she should mind her own business and let the parents raise their kids as they see fit, even if it's not ideal. But given the extreme behavior of the parents—yelling at Tj, grounding him, taking away his phone for two weeks, and not punishing Ked for stealing—it's hard to justify letting them continue without any intervention.

Moreover, she's not taking the phone to keep it for herself or to control Tj. She's holding onto it as a form of support for Tj, ensuring that the parents can't use it as a tool of punishment. She's essentially protecting Tj from further harm by the parents.

In conclusion, while some might see her action as overstepping, considering the parents' unfair and harmful behavior, her decision to take back the phone to protect Tj seems morally acceptable.
